stances_toward.note: Treaty ally (Article 5) since 1999 and the cabinet says it will honour its commitments; the friction is the bill. Defence reached 2% in 2024 and stayed at 2% in 2025 under Fiala, who set a path to 3% by 2030; the 2026 budget is about 1.78% by NATO's method (the government says 2.06%), Babiš says Czechia is 'certainly not' on a path to 3.5% and will reach 2% only in 2027. NATO is also where the cabinet would like Ukraine's ammunition financing to move. The grade stays ally: no source, including the Ankara summit assessments, questions membership. Bond - affinity: accession in 1999 and the post-1989 choice.

stances_toward.note: Partnership for Peace since 1994 and a cooperation programme with NATO; the 2023 strategy names NATO as a partner for strengthening the army and lists NATO members France, Germany, Poland, Italy, the Czech Republic, the Baltics and Turkey as 'security and defense partners'. No membership bid: neutrality is constitutional, Sandu said in 2023 that any change must come by democratic process, and polls give NATO membership 20-30% support. Stable because it is a ceiling set by the constitution, not by rhetoric. Bond - none: pure interest.
